page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several general computing and memory tasks. The instance achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, software compilation with Clang, and PassMark database operations. However, raw CPU throughput is a notable tradeoff; stress-ng single-core performance is in the bottom 10%, and multi-core performance falls in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks is also weak, though small-block cached read bandwidth remains average.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive, sustained CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and static web serving, where its average database and Redis SET performance can be leveraged without incurring the higher costs of compute-heavy instances.
